3	description: Empirical result — domain-retrained yolo26n (nc=4) is faster on DX-M1 NPU than stock (nc=80); INT8 NPU mAP ≈ fp32 GPU

10	YOLO26n African-wildlife DeepX showcase (2026-06-10, built via Ultralytics one-shot
11	`format=deepx` from `dx-runtime/venv-dx-runtime` which already bundles ultralytics[deepx
12	fork] + dx_com + dx_engine + torch+cuda — no separate install needed).
13	
14	Two non-obvious empirical findings worth reusing:
15	
16	1. **INT8 quantization was effectively lossless**: retrained model scored mAP50-95
17	   0.792 fp32 (GPU train val) and 0.791 INT8 on DX-M1 NPU. The DeepX EMA calibration on
18	   the domain images preserved accuracy.
19	
20	2. **The domain model (nc=4) ran FASTER on the NPU than the stock COCO model (nc=80)**:
21	   80.5 vs 57.0 FPS (12.4 vs 17.5 ms/img), same yolo26n backbone, both INT8 batch=1.
22	   Cause = smaller detection head + lighter on-device decode (4 class channels vs 80).
23	   So fewer classes ⇒ measurably higher NPU FPS, independent of accuracy. Confirmed by
24	   re-measuring baseline on an idle host (ruled out GPU-train contention).
25	
26	Stock COCO yolo26n mAP50-95 on african-wildlife ≈ 0.001 (class/index mismatch) — expected,
27	demonstrates why domain fine-tuning is needed. See [[project_ultralytics_deepx_integration]].
28	Measurement path: `YOLO(<deepx_dir>).val(data=..., split=val, batch=1, device='cpu')`;
29	FPS = 1000 / metrics.speed['inference'].

---
name: project_yolo26n_awildlife_showcase_finding
description: Empirical result — domain-retrained yolo26n (nc=4) is faster on DX-M1 NPU than stock (nc=80); INT8 NPU mAP ≈ fp32 GPU
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 04f4494e-a3c7-40db-96ca-457058ca3977
---

YOLO26n African-wildlife DeepX showcase (2026-06-10, built via Ultralytics one-shot
`format=deepx` from `dx-runtime/venv-dx-runtime` which already bundles ultralytics[deepx
fork] + dx_com + dx_engine + torch+cuda — no separate install needed).

Two non-obvious empirical findings worth reusing:

1. **INT8 quantization was effectively lossless**: retrained model scored mAP50-95
   0.792 fp32 (GPU train val) and 0.791 INT8 on DX-M1 NPU. The DeepX EMA calibration on
   the domain images preserved accuracy.

2. **The domain model (nc=4) ran FASTER on the NPU than the stock COCO model (nc=80)**:
   80.5 vs 57.0 FPS (12.4 vs 17.5 ms/img), same yolo26n backbone, both INT8 batch=1.
   Cause = smaller detection head + lighter on-device decode (4 class channels vs 80).
   So fewer classes ⇒ measurably higher NPU FPS, independent of accuracy. Confirmed by
   re-measuring baseline on an idle host (ruled out GPU-train contention).

Stock COCO yolo26n mAP50-95 on african-wildlife ≈ 0.001 (class/index mismatch) — expected,
demonstrates why domain fine-tuning is needed. See [[project_ultralytics_deepx_integration]].
Measurement path: `YOLO(<deepx_dir>).val(data=..., split=val, batch=1, device='cpu')`;
FPS = 1000 / metrics.speed['inference'].

1	# DEEPX DX-COM Compiler — Claude Code Entry Point
2	
3	> Self-contained entry point for Claude Code / OpenCode. Read this file first.
4	
5	## Response Language
6	
7	Match your response language to the user's prompt language — when asking questions
8	or responding, use the same language the user is using.
9	
10	**Technical term rule**: When responding in Korean, keep English technical terms in
11	their original English form. Do NOT transliterate English terms into Korean phonetics
12	(한글 음차 표기 금지). Established Korean loanwords (모델, 서버, 파일, 데이터) are acceptable. <!-- KOREAN-OK: rule text intentionally references Korean notation terms that agents must recognize -->
13	
14	## Recommended Model (Pre-Flight Check)
15	
16	DX Agentic Development requires strong instruction following and knowledge base
17	utilization. Before starting any task, check if you are running as one of the
18	recommended models:
19	
20	- **Claude Sonnet 4.6** or later
21	- **Claude Opus 4.6** or later
22	
23	If you are NOT one of these models (e.g., GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, Gemini, etc.),
24	output the following notice at the beginning of your first response:
25	
26	```
27	══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
28	⚠  DX-AGENTIC-DEV: MODEL NOTICE
29	
30	DX Agentic Development recommends Claude Sonnet 4.6+ or
31	Opus 4.6+. Your current model may produce lower quality
32	in instruction following, knowledge base utilization, and
33	API accuracy. Please switch to a recommended model.
34	══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
35	```
36	
37	After the box notice, proceed with the task normally. This is an informational
38	warning, not a blocking gate.
39	
40	### Model Notice Repeat (Non-Recommended Model Only)
41	
42	If you output the MODEL NOTICE box above (i.e., you are NOT a recommended model),
43	you MUST also output this shortened reminder **immediately before the actual question
44	line** that the user needs to answer — NOT at the beginning of the brainstorming flow.
45	
46	**Timing**: After all file reading, context analysis, and preamble text, right before
47	the line that contains the `?` (the actual question), insert this reminder:
48	
49	```
50	---
51	⚠ **Non-recommended model** — output quality may be degraded. Recommended: Claude Sonnet 4.6+ / Opus 4.6+
52	---
53	```
54	
55	**Example — WRONG** (repeat scrolls past with the box):
56	```
57	[DX-AGENTIC-DEV: START]
58	══ MODEL NOTICE ══
59	---  ⚠ Non-recommended model ---     ← TOO EARLY, scrolls past
60	... (reads files, analyzes context) ...
61	First question: ...?
62	```
63	
64	**Example — CORRECT** (repeat appears right before the question):
65	```
66	[DX-AGENTIC-DEV: START]
67	══ MODEL NOTICE ══
68	... (reads files, analyzes context) ...
69	---  ⚠ Non-recommended model ---     ← RIGHT BEFORE the question
70	First question: ...?
71	```
72	
73	Only output this reminder ONCE (before the first question), not before every question.
74	
75	## Skill Router — Universal Pre-Flight (HARD GATE)
76	
77	`/dx-skill-router` MUST be invoked as the **absolute first action** for
78	**every user message** — regardless of task type (development, analysis,
79	reading, explanation, or clarification).
80	
81	This rule applies before:
82	- Any file read or codebase exploration
83	- Any response or clarifying question
84	- Any SWE gate check or path classification
85	- Any code generation or plan creation
86	
87	**No exceptions.** The following rationalizations are ALL prohibited:
88	
89	| Rationalization | Reality |
90	|----------------|---------|
91	| "This is just reading/analyzing files" | Reading IS a task. Invoke router first. |
92	| "The user only asked a question" | Questions are tasks. Invoke router first. |
93	| "This is not a development task" | Router applies to ALL tasks, not only dev. |
94	| "I'll check for skills after I understand the request" | Check BEFORE understanding. |
95	| "This doesn't trigger SWE gates" | SWE gates are separate. Router is universal. |
96	
97	## Shared Knowledge
98	
99	All skills, instructions, toolsets, and memory live in `.deepx/`.
100	Read `.deepx/README.md` for the complete master index.
101	
102	## Critical Rule: Model Acquisition and End-to-End Compilation
103	
104	**MANDATORY**: When a user requests model compilation and does NOT provide a local
105	`.pt`, `.pth`, or `.onnx` file path, the agent MUST:
106	
107	1. **Identify the official download source** for the requested model
108	2. **Actually download** the model file to the session working directory
109	3. **Actually compile** the model through the full pipeline (PT→ONNX→DXNN or ONNX→DXNN)
110	4. **Produce a real `.dxnn` output file**
111	
112	**NEVER** stop at generating only a `config.json` or providing compilation
113	instructions. The user expects a compiled `.dxnn` model, not a recipe.
114	
115	### Model Download Sources (Priority Order)
116	
117	| Model Family | Source | Download Method |
118	|---|---|---|
119	| Ultralytics YOLO (v5-v12, v26) | GitHub Releases / `ultralytics` pip | `from ultralytics import YOLO; model = YOLO("yolo11n.pt")` or `wget` from releases |
120	| TorchVision (ResNet, MobileNet, etc.) | PyTorch Hub / torchvision | `torchvision.models.resnet50(weights="DEFAULT")` |
121	| Timm models | `timm` pip | `timm.create_model("efficientnet_b0", pretrained=True)` |
122	| ONNX Model Zoo | GitHub onnx/models | `wget` from tagged releases |
123	| Hugging Face | Hugging Face Hub | `huggingface_hub.hf_hub_download()` |
124	
125	### Anti-Patterns (NEVER Do)
126	
127	- Generating config.json and telling user "run dxcom yourself"
128	- Providing download URLs without actually downloading
129	- Stopping after ONNX export without compiling to DXNN
130	- Telling user to "install ultralytics and export" instead of doing it
131	- Producing only instructions instead of actual compiled artifacts
132	
133	## Interactive Workflow (MUST FOLLOW)
134	
135	**Always walk through key decisions with the user before compiling.** Ask 2-3 targeted
136	questions to confirm model format, target device, and calibration method (EMA or MinMax).
137	This creates a collaborative workflow and catches misunderstandings early. Only skip
138	questions if the user explicitly says "just compile it" or "use defaults".
139	
140	## Target Hardware (MANDATORY)
141	
142	Target device is always DX-M1 (`dx_m1`). Do NOT ask the user to select target
143	hardware. The dx-compiler only supports DX-M1. Ignore any parent-level configuration
144	that mentions DX-M1A — DX-M1A is discontinued and no longer supported.
145	
146	## Quantization — INT8 Only (MANDATORY)
147	
148	DX-COM always quantizes to INT8. There is no FP16/FP32 output option in the CLI,
149	Python API, or JSON config. Do NOT ask the user to choose output precision.
150	The only user-facing quantization choices are:
151	- **Calibration method**: `ema` (default) or `minmax`
152	- **Enhanced quantization scheme**: `DXQ-P0` through `DXQ-P5` (optional)
153	- **Calibration sample count** (default: 100)
154	
155	Do NOT ask "which precision?" or offer INT8/FP16/FP32 as choices.
156	
157	**Gate 1 — Brainstorm**: Confirm inputs (model path, format, target device, calibration data).
158	**Gate 2 — Build**: Execute compilation with chosen parameters.
159	**Gate 3 — Verify**: Validate output with DX-TRON, review compiler.log.
160	
161	## Quick Reference
162	
163	```bash
164	pip install dx-com                     # Install DX-COM compiler
165	dxcom --help                           # CLI help
166	dxcom -m model.onnx -c config.json -o output/   # Basic compilation
167	pytest tests/                          # Run tests
168	```
169	
170	```python
171	import dx_com
172	dx_com.compile(model="model.onnx", output_dir="output/", config="config.json")
173	```
174	
175	## Sample Model Workflow
176	
177	Test the full compilation pipeline with pre-built sample models:
178	
179	```bash
180	cd dx-compiler
181	./example/1-download_sample_models.sh      # Download ONNX + JSON configs
182	./example/2-download_sample_calibration_dataset.sh  # Download calibration dataset
183	./example/3-compile_sample_models.sh       # Compile all sample models to .dxnn
184	```
185	
186	Sample models: YOLOV5S-1, YOLOV5S_Face-1, MobileNetV2-1.
187	The downloaded JSON configs serve as canonical references when generating
188	config.json for new models — read a sample JSON of a similar model type.
189	
190	## Skills
191	
192	| Command | Description |
193	|---------|-------------|
194	| `/dx-agentic-compiler-convert` | Convert PyTorch model to ONNX |
195	| `/dx-agentic-compiler-compile` | Compile ONNX model to DXNN |
196	| `/dx-agentic-compiler-validate` | Validate compilation output |
197	| `/dx-swe-brainstorm` | Brainstorm, propose 2-3 approaches, spec self-review, then plan |
198	| `/dx-swe-tdd` | Validation-driven development with optional Red-Green-Refactor for unit tests |
199	| `/dx-swe-verify` | Process: verify before claiming completion — evidence before assertions |
200	| `/dx-swe-writing-plans` | Write implementation plans with bite-sized tasks |
201	| `/dx-swe-executing-plans` | Execute plans with review checkpoints |
202	| `/dx-swe-subagent-dev` | Execute plans via fresh subagent per task with two-stage review |
203	| `/dx-swe-debugging` | Systematic debugging — 4-phase root cause investigation before proposing fixes |
204	| `/dx-swe-receiving-review` | Evaluate code review feedback with technical rigor |
205	| `/dx-swe-requesting-review` | Request code review after completing features |
206	| `/dx-skill-router` | Skill discovery and invocation — check skills before any action |
207	| `/dx-harness-writing-skills` | Create and edit skill files |
208	| `/dx-swe-parallel-agents` | Dispatch parallel subagents for independent tasks |
209	
210	## Critical Conventions
211	
212	1. **Batch size must be 1**: DEEPX NPU only supports batch=1
213	2. **Static shapes only**: No dynamic axes, no -1 dimensions
214	3. **ONNX opset 11-21**: Use opset 13 for best compatibility
215	4. **Input name match**: config.json `inputs` key must exactly match ONNX input name
216	5. **Representative calibration**: Calibration images must match inference distribution
217	6. **PPU type matters**: Type 0 = anchor-based (YOLOv3-v7), Type 1 = anchor-free (YOLOX, YOLOv8-v12). YOLO26 does not support PPU.
218	7. **Always validate**: Run DX-TRON inspection after every compilation
219	8. **No hardcoded paths**: Use parameters or environment variables for all paths
220	9. **No auto-simplification**: Do NOT run `onnx-simplifier` unless the user explicitly requests it — risks include numerical precision loss, node name changes breaking config.json, and potential model breakage
221	10. **Ultralytics YOLO export**: Must set `Detect.export=True` or use `model.export(format="onnx")` — standard `torch.onnx.export()` produces 6 outputs instead of 1. Always verify ONNX has exactly 1 output node after export.
222	11. **MANDATORY brainstorming questions**: Before any compilation task, the agent MUST ask three mandatory questions: (Q1) NMS-free model detection with YOLO version characteristics table, (Q2) ONNX simplification with pros/cons explanation, (Q3) PPU compilation support with hardware vs flexibility trade-off. See `.deepx/agents/dx-compiler-builder.md` Step 2 for the exact question templates.
223	12. **PPU default is OFF**: PPU compilation is opt-in. Only add PPU config to config.json if the user explicitly confirms during brainstorming Q3. **YOLO26 does not support PPU** — skip Q3 for YOLO26 models (NMS-free native architecture).
224	13. **Model Acquisition — download and compile, not just instruct**: If the user does not provide a local `.pt`/`.pth`/`.onnx` file, the agent MUST find the official download source (Ultralytics releases, torchvision, timm, ONNX Model Zoo, Hugging Face), actually download the model, and compile it through the full pipeline to produce a `.dxnn` file. NEVER stop at generating only config.json or providing compilation instructions.

247	
248	All compilation artifacts go to `dx-agentic-dev/<session_id>/` by default. Each
249	compilation session uses a unique working directory to keep artifacts together and
250	prevent overwrites.
251	
252	**Session ID format**: `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS_<agent>_<coding_model>_<target_model>_<task>` — the timestamp MUST use the
253	**system local timezone** (NOT UTC). Use `$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)` in Bash or
254	`datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')` in Python. Do NOT use `date -u`,
255	`datetime.utcnow()`, or `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`.
256	- **`<agent>`**: the coding agent identifier — use `claude`, `codex`, `copilot`, `cursor`, or `opencode`.
257	- **`<coding_model>`**: shortened coding model name — e.g., `sonnet46`, `opus46`, `gpt53codex`, `gpt55`.

312	## Ultralytics → DeepX Export (One-Shot Path)
313	
314	Ultralytics YOLO ships a first-class `format=deepx` exporter that produces a
315	deployable DeepX NPU model in **one command** — it runs ONNX export → INT8 EMA
316	calibration → `dx_com` compilation → packaging internally:
317	
318	```bash
319	yolo export model=yolo26n.pt format=deepx     # creates 'yolo26n_deepx_model/'
320	```
321	```python
322	from ultralytics import YOLO
323	YOLO("yolo26n.pt").export(format="deepx")      # int8=True is enforced
324	```
325	
326	**Prefer this path** for Ultralytics YOLO **detection** models targeting DeepX —
327	it avoids the common manual PT→ONNX→`dxcom` errors. Fall back to the manual
328	pipeline (`dx-agentic-compiler-convert` → `dxcom`) only for non-detection tasks,
329	non-YOLO/custom graphs, or when fine control over `config.json` is required.
330	
331	Key facts (full reference: `.deepx/toolsets/ultralytics-deepx-export.md`):
332	
333	- **x86-64 Linux only** for export (`dx_com` has no ARM64); **detection only**; **INT8 enforced**.
334	- Output is a **directory** `<model>_deepx_model/` = `{<model>.dxnn, config.json, metadata.yaml}` — not a bare `.dxnn`.
335	- Calibration: EMA, default 100 images (`data` / `fraction` to tune).
336	- Deploy: `YOLO("<model>_deepx_model")` → `model(source)` on the `dx_engine` runtime
337	  (backend converts BCHW float `[0,1]` → HWC uint8 `[0,255]`). Inference is not ARM64-restricted.
338	- `dx_com` auto-installs via Ultralytics' export (version pinned by the installed
339	  `ultralytics` release). **Do NOT manually `pip install dx-com` from a hardcoded SDK
340	  URL/version** — it pins a stale compiler; to update, upgrade `ultralytics`.
341	- **Deployment prerequisite**: the `dx_engine` **runtime** is end-user-installed —
342	  Ultralytics auto-installs it **only on Debian Trixie/arm64** (sixfab-dx). On the
343	  x86-64 dx-all-suite the backend raises `OSError: dx_engine is not installed. … Please
344	  install dx_engine manually and try again` → here "install manually" = **install the
345	  `dx_rt` runtime** (provides `dxrt-cli`+`dx_engine`): `dx-runtime/scripts/sanity_check.sh
346	  --dx_rt`, then `dx-runtime/install.sh --all --exclude-app --exclude-stream
347	  --skip-uninstall --venv-reuse` (dx_app/dx_stream NOT needed → skip to save time), retry.
348	  NPU init failure → cold boot. Never `pip install dx_engine` on x86-64 or fake via PYTHONPATH.

582	
583	When a user's request conflicts with a HARD GATE rule, the agent MUST:
584

596	  calls are handled internally by SyncRunner/AsyncRunner; implement the 5 IFactory

622	files is fine — committing them is forbidden.
623	
624	## Session Sentinels (MANDATORY for Automated Testing)
625	
626	When processing a user prompt, output these exact markers for automated session
627	boundary detection by the test harness:
628	
629	- **First line of your response**: `[DX-AGENTIC-DEV: START]`
630	- **Last line after ALL work is complete**: `[DX-AGENTIC-DEV: DONE (output-dir: <relative_path>)]`
631	  where `<relative_path>` is the session output directory (e.g., `dx-agentic-dev/20260409-143022_yolo26n_detection/`)
632	
633	### DEEPX Banner (MANDATORY — print with the sentinels)
634	
635	Render the DEEPX logo banner **verbatim** at two points: **immediately after** the
636	`[DX-AGENTIC-DEV: START]` line, and **immediately before** the
637	`[DX-AGENTIC-DEV: DONE ...]` line. Print it exactly as below (a fenced block is fine):
638	
639	```
640	 ███████████   █████████ ████████ ████████  ████      ████
641	 ███     █████ ███░░░░░░░███░░░░░░███   ███  ░████   ████░░
642	 ███        ██░███░      ██░░     ███   ███░   █████████░░
643	 ███        ████████████ ████████ ████████░░    ░█████░░░
644	 ███        ██░███░░░░░░░██░░░░░░░███░░░░░░  ██████████
645	 ███     █████░███░      ██░      ███░   ████████░░░░████
646	 ███████████░░░█████████ ████████ ██████████░░░░░░    ████
647	  ░░░░░░░░░░░   ░░░░░░░░░ ░░░░░░░░ ░░░░░░░░░░          ░░░░
648	        DX-AGENTIC-DEV · on-device NPU
649	```
650	
651	The banner is decorative; it never replaces or moves the sentinel lines (START stays
652	the absolute first line, DONE stays the very last line).
653	
654	Rules:
655	1. **CRITICAL — Output `[DX-AGENTIC-DEV: START]` as the absolute first line of your
656	   first response.** This must appear before ANY other text, tool calls, or reasoning.
657	   Even if the user instructs you to "just proceed" or "use your own judgment",
658	   the START sentinel is non-negotiable — automated tests WILL fail without it.
659	   **Immediately after the START line, print the DEEPX banner** (see "DEEPX Banner" above).
660	2. **Immediately before the DONE line, print the DEEPX banner again**, then output
661	   `[DX-AGENTIC-DEV: DONE (output-dir: <path>)]` as the very last line after all work,
662	   validation, and file generation is complete
663	3. If you are a **sub-agent** invoked via handoff/routing from a higher-level agent,
664	   do NOT output these sentinels — only the top-level agent outputs them
665	4. If the user sends multiple prompts in a session, output START/DONE for each prompt
666	5. The `output-dir` in DONE must be the relative path from the project root to the
667	   session output directory. If no files were generated, omit the `(output-dir: ...)` part.
668	   **For cross-project tasks** (e.g., compile + app generation), list ALL output directories
669	   separated by ` + `:
670	   ```
671	   [DX-AGENTIC-DEV: DONE (output-dir: dx-compiler/dx-agentic-dev/20260409-143022_copilot_yolo26n_compile/ + dx-runtime/dx_app/dx-agentic-dev/20260409-143022_copilot_yolo26n_inference/)]
672	   ```
673	6. **NEVER output DONE after only producing planning artifacts** (specs, plans, design
674	   documents). DONE means all deliverables are produced — implementation code, scripts,
675	   configs, and validation results. If you completed a brainstorming or planning phase
676	   but have not yet implemented the actual code, do NOT output DONE. Instead, proceed
677	   to implementation or ask the user how to proceed.
678	7. **Pre-DONE mandatory deliverable check**: Before outputting DONE, verify that all
679	   mandatory deliverables exist in the session directory. If any mandatory file is
680	   missing, create it before outputting DONE. Each sub-project defines its own mandatory
681	   file list in its skill document (e.g., `dx-agentic-stream-build-pipeline.md` File Creation Checklist).
682	8. **Session transcript — generate it RIGHT AFTER the DONE line (claude / copilot)**:
683	
684	   **Auto-transcript is supported on `claude` and `copilot` only.** Emit the DONE
685	   sentinel line FIRST, then — as the single final housekeeping step — render this
686	   session's transcript with the shared generator **directly into the session output
687	   dir(s)** (the same dir(s) you listed in DONE). Running it *after* DONE means the
688	   CLI's session store has already committed the DONE turn, so the rendered transcript
689	   is complete (rendering *before* DONE truncates the tail). Needs **no hook**:
690	
691	   ```bash
692	   # Locate the shared generator by walking up to the suite root: GENROOT is the dir
693	   # that contains .deepx/tools. Then render THIS session's transcript INTO the session
694	   # output dir(s). Pass EVERY output dir you created (the transcript is copied into each
695	   # — cross-project: both the compiler and app dirs). The session id is auto-resolved
696	   # from this CLI's own env var (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID / COPILOT_AGENT_SESSION_ID).
697	   #
698	   # CRITICAL — use ABSOLUTE paths for --project AND --into-output-dirs. A RELATIVE
699	   # output dir is resolved against the agent's CURRENT cwd, so it is SILENTLY SKIPPED
700	   # ("no output dir produced — transcript generation skipped") whenever cwd is not the
701	   # suite root — e.g. after you cd into the session dir to run setup.sh/run.sh. Prefix
702	   # every output dir with "$GENROOT/" (or pass the same absolute SESSION_DIR you used
703	   # to write artifacts).
704	   GENROOT="$(d="$PWD"; while [ "$d" != / ]; do [ -f "$d/.deepx/tools/src/dx_transcripts/generate_transcripts.py" ] && { echo "$d"; break; }; d="$(dirname "$d")"; done)"
705	   GT="$GENROOT/.deepx/tools/src/dx_transcripts/generate_transcripts.py"
706	   python3 "$GT" --tool <CLI> --project "$GENROOT" \
707	       --into-output-dirs "$GENROOT/<output-dir>" ["$GENROOT/<output-dir-2>" ...]
708	   ```
709	
710	   `<CLI>` is `claude` or `copilot`. The generator reuses the **same renderers as the
711	   test harness** (`parse_<tool>_session`) and writes `<CLI>-session.md` +
712	   `<CLI>-session.html` + `<CLI>-stream.jsonl` into each output dir. **If you produced
713	   NO output dir** (e.g. a pure question with no files), pass no dir and generation is
714	   **skipped** — expected, not an error. After it runs, state the path on the final
715	   line, e.g. `Session transcript (md/html/jsonl) saved to: <output-dir>/<CLI>-session.*`.
716	
717	   > **Known limitation — the in-session transcript is store-based and therefore
718	   > incomplete.** Run from inside the live session, the generator reads the session
719	   > **store**, which has NO synthetic `result` event — that event (carrying
720	   > `duration_ms` → *Wall-clock* and `total_cost_usd` → *Cost*) exists only in the
721	   > `claude -p --output-format stream-json` **stdout**, emitted at process exit. The
722	   > render also happens *during* the transcript tool-call, so it truncates just before
723	   > this very "saved to …" narration. Net effect: the in-session transcript **omits
724	   > Wall-clock + Cost and the closing narration** — expected, not a bug. For a
725	   > **complete** transcript (Wall-clock + Cost + tail, like the showcase ones),
726	   > capture the run's stdout and render it externally **after** the process exits:
727	   > `python3 "$GT" --tool <CLI> --session-id <uuid> --project "$GENROOT" --stream-json <captured-stdout.jsonl> --out-dir <output-dir>`
728	   > (the test harness / build recorders do this). An in-session agent cannot — it has
729	   > no handle on its own stdout stream.
730	
731	   **`codex`, `opencode`, `cursor` are NOT auto-supported** — do NOT run the generator
732	   in-session for them (it cannot produce a complete/usable transcript: codex and
733	   opencode commit their final turn only at process exit; cursor redacts the assistant
734	   text in its store). Instead, tell the user how to generate it manually:
735	   - **codex / opencode**: after the session ends, run
736	     `python3 <generate_transcripts.py> --tool <codex|opencode> --project . --out-dir <DIR>`
737	     — the finalized store then renders a complete transcript.
738	   - **cursor**: capture the run with `agent -p --output-format stream-json > run.jsonl`
739	     and render with `--tool cursor --stream-json run.jsonl`, or use IDE session history.
740	   (If you invoke the generator with `--into-output-dirs` on these tools, it safely
741	   skips and prints this same guidance — that is expected.)
742	
743	## Plan Output (MANDATORY)
744	
745	When generating a plan document (e.g., via writing-plans or brainstorming skills),
746	**always print the full plan content in the conversation output** immediately after
747	saving the file. Do NOT only mention the file path — the user should be able to
748	review the plan directly in the prompt without opening a separate file.
749	
750	
751	---
752	
753	## Instruction File Verification Loop (HARD GATE) — Internal Development Only
754	
755	When modifying the canonical source — files in `**/.deepx/**/*.md`
756	(agents, skills, templates, fragments) — the following verify-fix loop is
757	**MANDATORY** before claiming work is complete:
758	
759	1. **Generator execution** — Propagate `.deepx/` changes to all platforms:
760	   ```bash
761	   dx-agentic-gen generate
762	   # Suite-wide: bash .deepx/tools/scripts/run_all.sh generate
763	   ```
764	2. **Drift verification** — Confirm generated output matches committed state:
765	   ```bash
766	   dx-agentic-gen check
767	   ```
768	   If drift is detected, return to step 1.
769	3. **Automated test loop** — Tests verify generator output satisfies policies:
770	   ```bash
771	   python -m pytest .deepx/tests/conformance/ .deepx/tools/tests/ -v --tb=short
772	   ```
773	   Failure handling:
774	   - Generator bug → fix generator → step 1
775	   - `.deepx/` content gap → fix `.deepx/` → step 1
776	   - Insufficient test rules → strengthen tests → step 1
777	4. **Manual audit** — Independently (without relying on test results) read
778	   generated files to verify cross-platform sync (CLAUDE vs AGENTS vs copilot)
779	   and level-to-level sync (suite → sub-levels).
780	5. **Gap analysis** — For issues found by manual audit:
781	   - Generator missed a case → **fix generator rules** → step 1
782	   - Tests missed a case → **strengthen tests** → step 1
783	6. **Repeat** — Continue until steps 3–5 all pass.
784	
785	### Pre-flight Classification (MANDATORY)
786	
787	Before modifying ANY `.md` or `.mdc` file in the repository, classify it into
788	one of three categories. **Never skip this step** — editing a generator-managed
789	file directly is a silent corruption that will be overwritten on next generate.
790	
791	**Answer these three questions in order before every file edit:**
792	
793	> **Q1. Is the file path inside `**/.deepx/**`?**
794	> - YES → **Canonical source.** Edit directly, then run `dx-agentic-gen generate` + `check`.
795	> - NO → go to Q2.
796	>
797	> **Q2. Does the file path or name match any of these?**
798	> ```
799	> .github/agents/    .github/skills/    .opencode/agents/
800	> .claude/agents/    .claude/skills/    .cursor/rules/
801	> CLAUDE.md          CLAUDE-KO.md       AGENTS.md    AGENTS-KO.md
802	> copilot-instructions.md               copilot-instructions-KO.md
803	> ```
804	> - YES → **Generator output. DO NOT edit directly.**
805	>   Find the `.deepx/` source (template, fragment, or agent/skill) and edit that instead,
806	>   then run `dx-agentic-gen generate`.
807	> - NO → go to Q3.
808	>
809	> **Q3. Does the file begin with `<!-- AUTO-GENERATED`?**
810	> - YES → **Generator output. DO NOT edit directly.** Same as Q2.
811	> - NO → **Independent source.** Edit directly. Run `dx-agentic-gen check` once afterward.
812	
813	1. **Canonical source** (`**/.deepx/**/*.md`) — Modify directly, then run the
814	   Verification Loop above.
815	2. **Generator output** — Files at known output paths:
816	   `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE-KO.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS-KO.md`,
817	   `copilot-instructions.md`, `.github/agents/`, `.github/skills/`,
818	   `.claude/agents/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.opencode/agents/`, `.cursor/rules/`
819	   → **Do NOT edit directly.** Find and modify the `.deepx/` source
820	   (template, fragment, or agent/skill), then `dx-agentic-gen generate`.
821	3. **Independent source** — Everything else (`docs/source/`, `source/docs/`,
822	   `tests/`, `README.md` in sub-projects, etc.)
823	   → Edit directly. Run `dx-agentic-gen check` once afterward to confirm no
824	   unexpected drift.
825	
826	**Anti-pattern**: Modifying a file without first classifying it. If you are
827	unsure whether a file is generator output, run `dx-agentic-gen check` before
828	AND after the edit — if the check overwrites your change, the file is managed
829	by the generator and must be edited via `.deepx/` source instead.
830	
831	A pre-commit hook enforces generator output integrity: `git commit` will fail
832	if generated files are out-of-date. Install hooks with:
833	```bash
834	.deepx/tools/scripts/install-hooks.sh
835	```
836	
837	> **KO counterpart rule**: When editing any EN fragment, check whether the KO
838	> counterpart also needs updating. If you added or removed ≥ 1 paragraph, update
839	> `.deepx/templates/fragments/ko/<stem>.md` before committing. Run
840	> `dx-agentic-gen lint` to verify `[OK]` — lint will ERROR if EN exceeds KO by
841	> ≥ 10 lines.
842	
843	This gate applies when `.deepx/` files are the *primary deliverable* (e.g., adding
844	rules, syncing platforms, creating KO translations, modifying agents/skills). It
845	does NOT apply when a feature implementation incidentally triggers a single-line
846	change in `.deepx/`.

# DEEPX DX-COM Compiler — Claude Code Entry Point

> Self-contained entry point for Claude Code / OpenCode. Read this file first.

## Response Language

Match your response language to the user's prompt language — when asking questions
or responding, use the same language the user is using.

**Technical term rule**: When responding in Korean, keep English technical terms in
their original English form. Do NOT transliterate English terms into Korean phonetics
(한글 음차 표기 금지). Established Korean loanwords (모델, 서버, 파일, 데이터) are acceptable. <!-- KOREAN-OK: rule text intentionally references Korean notation terms that agents must recognize -->

## Recommended Model (Pre-Flight Check)

DX Agentic Development requires strong instruction following and knowledge base
utilization. Before starting any task, check if you are running as one of the
recommended models:

- **Claude Sonnet 4.6** or later
- **Claude Opus 4.6** or later

If you are NOT one of these models (e.g., GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, Gemini, etc.),
output the following notice at the beginning of your first response:

```
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
⚠  DX-AGENTIC-DEV: MODEL NOTICE

DX Agentic Development recommends Claude Sonnet 4.6+ or
Opus 4.6+. Your current model may produce lower quality
in instruction following, knowledge base utilization, and
API accuracy. Please switch to a recommended model.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

After the box notice, proceed with the task normally. This is an informational
warning, not a blocking gate.

### Model Notice Repeat (Non-Recommended Model Only)

If you output the MODEL NOTICE box above (i.e., you are NOT a recommended model),
you MUST also output this shortened reminder **immediately before the actual question
line** that the user needs to answer — NOT at the beginning of the brainstorming flow.

**Timing**: After all file reading, context analysis, and preamble text, right before
the line that contains the `?` (the actual question), insert this reminder:

```
---
⚠ **Non-recommended model** — output quality may be degraded. Recommended: Claude Sonnet 4.6+ / Opus 4.6+
---
```

**Example — WRONG** (repeat scrolls past with the box):
```
[DX-AGENTIC-DEV: START]
══ MODEL NOTICE ══
---  ⚠ Non-recommended model ---     ← TOO EARLY, scrolls past
... (reads files, analyzes context) ...
First question: ...?
```

**Example — CORRECT** (repeat appears right before the question):
```
[DX-AGENTIC-DEV: START]
══ MODEL NOTICE ══
... (reads files, analyzes context) ...
---  ⚠ Non-recommended model ---     ← RIGHT BEFORE the question
First question: ...?
```

Only output this reminder ONCE (before the first question), not before every question.

## Skill Router — Universal Pre-Flight (HARD GATE)

`/dx-skill-router` MUST be invoked as the **absolute first action** for
**every user message** — regardless of task type (development, analysis,
reading, explanation, or clarification).

This rule applies before:
- Any file read or codebase exploration
- Any response or clarifying question
- Any SWE gate check or path classification
- Any code generation or plan creation

**No exceptions.** The following rationalizations are ALL prohibited:

| Rationalization | Reality |
|----------------|---------|
| "This is just reading/analyzing files" | Reading IS a task. Invoke router first. |
| "The user only asked a question" | Questions are tasks. Invoke router first. |
| "This is not a development task" | Router applies to ALL tasks, not only dev. |
| "I'll check for skills after I understand the request" | Check BEFORE understanding. |
| "This doesn't trigger SWE gates" | SWE gates are separate. Router is universal. |

## Shared Knowledge

All skills, instructions, toolsets, and memory live in `.deepx/`.
Read `.deepx/README.md` for the complete master index.

## Critical Rule: Model Acquisition and End-to-End Compilation

**MANDATORY**: When a user requests model compilation and does NOT provide a local
`.pt`, `.pth`, or `.onnx` file path, the agent MUST:

1. **Identify the official download source** for the requested model
2. **Actually download** the model file to the session working directory
3. **Actually compile** the model through the full pipeline (PT→ONNX→DXNN or ONNX→DXNN)
4. **Produce a real `.dxnn` output file**

**NEVER** stop at generating only a `config.json` or providing compilation
instructions. The user expects a compiled `.dxnn` model, not a recipe.

### Model Download Sources (Priority Order)

| Model Family | Source | Download Method |
|---|---|---|
| Ultralytics YOLO (v5-v12, v26) | GitHub Releases / `ultralytics` pip | `from ultralytics import YOLO; model = YOLO("yolo11n.pt")` or `wget` from releases |
| TorchVision (ResNet, MobileNet, etc.) | PyTorch Hub / torchvision | `torchvision.models.resnet50(weights="DEFAULT")` |
| Timm models | `timm` pip | `timm.create_model("efficientnet_b0", pretrained=True)` |
| ONNX Model Zoo | GitHub onnx/models | `wget` from tagged releases |
| Hugging Face | Hugging Face Hub | `huggingface_hub.hf_hub_download()` |

### Anti-Patterns (NEVER Do)

- Generating config.json and telling user "run dxcom yourself"
- Providing download URLs without actually downloading
- Stopping after ONNX export without compiling to DXNN
- Telling user to "install ultralytics and export" instead of doing it
- Producing only instructions instead of actual compiled artifacts

## Interactive Workflow (MUST FOLLOW)

**Always walk through key decisions with the user before compiling.** Ask 2-3 targeted
questions to confirm model format, target device, and calibration method (EMA or MinMax).
This creates a collaborative workflow and catches misunderstandings early. Only skip
questions if the user explicitly says "just compile it" or "use defaults".

## Target Hardware (MANDATORY)

Target device is always DX-M1 (`dx_m1`). Do NOT ask the user to select target
hardware. The dx-compiler only supports DX-M1. Ignore any parent-level configuration
that mentions DX-M1A — DX-M1A is discontinued and no longer supported.

## Quantization — INT8 Only (MANDATORY)

DX-COM always quantizes to INT8. There is no FP16/FP32 output option in the CLI,
Python API, or JSON config. Do NOT ask the user to choose output precision.
The only user-facing quantization choices are:
- **Calibration method**: `ema` (default) or `minmax`
- **Enhanced quantization scheme**: `DXQ-P0` through `DXQ-P5` (optional)
- **Calibration sample count** (default: 100)

Do NOT ask "which precision?" or offer INT8/FP16/FP32 as choices.

**Gate 1 — Brainstorm**: Confirm inputs (model path, format, target device, calibration data).
**Gate 2 — Build**: Execute compilation with chosen parameters.
**Gate 3 — Verify**: Validate output with DX-TRON, review compiler.log.

## Quick Reference

```bash
pip install dx-com                     # Install DX-COM compiler
dxcom --help                           # CLI help
dxcom -m model.onnx -c config.json -o output/   # Basic compilation
pytest tests/                          # Run tests
```

```python
import dx_com
dx_com.compile(model="model.onnx", output_dir="output/", config="config.json")
```

## Sample Model Workflow

Test the full compilation pipeline with pre-built sample models:

```bash
cd dx-compiler
./example/1-download_sample_models.sh      # Download ONNX + JSON configs
./example/2-download_sample_calibration_dataset.sh  # Download calibration dataset
./example/3-compile_sample_models.sh       # Compile all sample models to .dxnn
```

Sample models: YOLOV5S-1, YOLOV5S_Face-1, MobileNetV2-1.
The downloaded JSON configs serve as canonical references when generating
config.json for new models — read a sample JSON of a similar model type.

## Skills

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `/dx-agentic-compiler-convert` | Convert PyTorch model to ONNX |
| `/dx-agentic-compiler-compile` | Compile ONNX model to DXNN |
| `/dx-agentic-compiler-validate` | Validate compilation output |
| `/dx-swe-brainstorm` | Brainstorm, propose 2-3 approaches, spec self-review, then plan |
| `/dx-swe-tdd` | Validation-driven development with optional Red-Green-Refactor for unit tests |
| `/dx-swe-verify` | Process: verify before claiming completion — evidence before assertions |
| `/dx-swe-writing-plans` | Write implementation plans with bite-sized tasks |
| `/dx-swe-executing-plans` | Execute plans with review checkpoints |
| `/dx-swe-subagent-dev` | Execute plans via fresh subagent per task with two-stage review |
| `/dx-swe-debugging` | Systematic debugging — 4-phase root cause investigation before proposing fixes |
| `/dx-swe-receiving-review` | Evaluate code review feedback with technical rigor |
| `/dx-swe-requesting-review` | Request code review after completing features |
| `/dx-skill-router` | Skill discovery and invocation — check skills before any action |
| `/dx-harness-writing-skills` | Create and edit skill files |
| `/dx-swe-parallel-agents` | Dispatch parallel subagents for independent tasks |

## Critical Conventions

1. **Batch size must be 1**: DEEPX NPU only supports batch=1
2. **Static shapes only**: No dynamic axes, no -1 dimensions
3. **ONNX opset 11-21**: Use opset 13 for best compatibility
4. **Input name match**: config.json `inputs` key must exactly match ONNX input name
5. **Representative calibration**: Calibration images must match inference distribution
6. **PPU type matters**: Type 0 = anchor-based (YOLOv3-v7), Type 1 = anchor-free (YOLOX, YOLOv8-v12). YOLO26 does not support PPU.
7. **Always validate**: Run DX-TRON inspection after every compilation
8. **No hardcoded paths**: Use parameters or environment variables for all paths
9. **No auto-simplification**: Do NOT run `onnx-simplifier` unless the user explicitly requests it — risks include numerical precision loss, node name changes breaking config.json, and potential model breakage
10. **Ultralytics YOLO export**: Must set `Detect.export=True` or use `model.export(format="onnx")` — standard `torch.onnx.export()` produces 6 outputs instead of 1. Always verify ONNX has exactly 1 output node after export.
11. **MANDATORY brainstorming questions**: Before any compilation task, the agent MUST ask three mandatory questions: (Q1) NMS-free model detection with YOLO version characteristics table, (Q2) ONNX simplification with pros/cons explanation, (Q3) PPU compilation support with hardware vs flexibility trade-off. See `.deepx/agents/dx-compiler-builder.md` Step 2 for the exact question templates.
12. **PPU default is OFF**: PPU compilation is opt-in. Only add PPU config to config.json if the user explicitly confirms during brainstorming Q3. **YOLO26 does not support PPU** — skip Q3 for YOLO26 models (NMS-free native architecture).
13. **Model Acquisition — download and compile, not just instruct**: If the user does not provide a local `.pt`/`.pth`/`.onnx` file, the agent MUST find the official download source (Ultralytics releases, torchvision, timm, ONNX Model Zoo, Hugging Face), actually download the model, and compile it through the full pipeline to produce a `.dxnn` file. NEVER stop at generating only config.json or providing compilation instructions.
14. **Post-compilation verification is MANDATORY — compilation is NOT complete without it**: After every successful `dxcom` compilation, the agent MUST complete ALL of the following before presenting results to the user. NEVER present a "compilation successful" summary without these:
    - **(a)** Generate `setup.sh`, `run.sh`, `README.md` in the output directory (session dir OR user-specified dir)
    - **(b)** Generate `verify.py` — ONNX vs DXNN inference comparison script
    - **(c)** Run `verify.py` and confirm PASS (detection count within 20%, classes match, IoU > 0.5)
    - **(d)** Save the session log to `${WORK_DIR}/session.log` — must contain **actual command execution output** captured via `tee`, NOT a hand-written summary
    - **(e)** Include verification results (PASS/FAIL) and all artifact paths in the final summary table
    - If any step fails, debug and fix before proceeding. The `.dxnn` file alone is NOT a deliverable.
    - **Even when the user specifies a custom output directory** (e.g., a source directory instead of `dx-agentic-dev/`), these artifacts are still MANDATORY.
15. **Never reuse previous session artifacts**: NEVER check, list, browse, or reuse artifacts from previous sessions in `dx-agentic-dev/`. Each compilation run MUST create a new session directory with a fresh timestamp. Even if a previous session compiled the same model, always re-download, re-export, and re-compile from scratch. Do NOT run `ls dx-agentic-dev/` or check for existing `.onnx`/`.dxnn` files from past runs.
16. **venv is MANDATORY in setup.sh**: Generated `setup.sh` MUST create and activate a virtual environment before any `pip install`. On Ubuntu 24.04+, PEP 668 blocks system-wide pip installs. Use `python3 -m venv` with `${VIRTUAL_ENV:-}` check. Generated `run.sh` MUST check venv activation and auto-activate or error if missing.
17. **Cross-validation with precompiled reference model**: When a precompiled DXNN for the same model exists in `dx-runtime/dx_app/assets/models/`, run verify.py with BOTH the precompiled and generated models (Phase 5.7). Both fail → verify.py bug. Precompiled passes, generated fails → compilation problem. See `.deepx/agents/dx-dxnn-compiler.md` Phase 5.7.
18. **NHWC/NCHW DataLoader mismatch**: The dxcom CLI's default dataloader loads images in NHWC `[1,H,W,C]`. If the ONNX model expects NCHW `[1,C,H,W]` (most PyTorch-exported models), CLI compilation will fail with `DataLoaderError: Input shape mismatch`. **Fix**: Use the Python API (`dx_com.compile()`) with a custom torch DataLoader that produces NCHW tensors. See `.deepx/memory/common_pitfalls.md` pitfall #18.

## Output Isolation

All compilation artifacts go to `dx-agentic-dev/<session_id>/` by default. Each
compilation session uses a unique working directory to keep artifacts together and
prevent overwrites.

**Session ID format**: `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS_<agent>_<coding_model>_<target_model>_<task>` — the timestamp MUST use the
**system local timezone** (NOT UTC). Use `$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)` in Bash or
`datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')` in Python. Do NOT use `date -u`,
`datetime.utcnow()`, or `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`.
- **`<agent>`**: the coding agent identifier — use `claude`, `codex`, `copilot`, `cursor`, or `opencode`.
- **`<coding_model>`**: shortened coding model name — e.g., `sonnet46`, `opus46`, `gpt53codex`, `gpt55`.

```bash
SESSION_ID="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)_yolo26x_onnx_to_dxnn"
WORK_DIR="dx-agentic-dev/${SESSION_ID}"
mkdir -p "${WORK_DIR}"

# Symlink calibration data into working directory
ln -sf ../../dx_com/calibration_dataset "${WORK_DIR}/calibration_dataset"

# config.json uses relative path: "dataset_path": "./calibration_dataset"
dxcom -m "${WORK_DIR}/model.onnx" -c "${WORK_DIR}/config.json" -o "${WORK_DIR}/"
```

**Working directory contents** after compilation:
```
dx-agentic-dev/<session_id>/
├── calibration_dataset   → ../../dx_com/calibration_dataset/ (symlink)
├── config.json
├── model.onnx
├── model.dxnn
├── compiler.log
└── README.md             (session report)
```

## Ultralytics → DeepX Export (One-Shot Path)

Ultralytics YOLO ships a first-class `format=deepx` exporter that produces a
deployable DeepX NPU model in **one command** — it runs ONNX export → INT8 EMA
calibration → `dx_com` compilation → packaging internally:

```bash
yolo export model=yolo26n.pt format=deepx     # creates 'yolo26n_deepx_model/'
```
```python
from ultralytics import YOLO
YOLO("yolo26n.pt").export(format="deepx")      # int8=True is enforced
```

**Prefer this path** for Ultralytics YOLO **detection** models targeting DeepX —
it avoids the common manual PT→ONNX→`dxcom` errors. Fall back to the manual
pipeline (`dx-agentic-compiler-convert` → `dxcom`) only for non-detection tasks,
non-YOLO/custom graphs, or when fine control over `config.json` is required.

Key facts (full reference: `.deepx/toolsets/ultralytics-deepx-export.md`):

- **x86-64 Linux only** for export (`dx_com` has no ARM64); **detection only**; **INT8 enforced**.
- Output is a **directory** `<model>_deepx_model/` = `{<model>.dxnn, config.json, metadata.yaml}` — not a bare `.dxnn`.
- Calibration: EMA, default 100 images (`data` / `fraction` to tune).
- Deploy: `YOLO("<model>_deepx_model")` → `model(source)` on the `dx_engine` runtime
  (backend converts BCHW float `[0,1]` → HWC uint8 `[0,255]`). Inference is not ARM64-restricted.
- `dx_com` auto-installs via Ultralytics' export (version pinned by the installed
  `ultralytics` release). **Do NOT manually `pip install dx-com` from a hardcoded SDK
  URL/version** — it pins a stale compiler; to update, upgrade `ultralytics`.
- **Deployment prerequisite**: the `dx_engine` **runtime** is end-user-installed —
  Ultralytics auto-installs it **only on Debian Trixie/arm64** (sixfab-dx). On the
  x86-64 dx-all-suite the backend raises `OSError: dx_engine is not installed. … Please
  install dx_engine manually and try again` → here "install manually" = **install the
  `dx_rt` runtime** (provides `dxrt-cli`+`dx_engine`): `dx-runtime/scripts/sanity_check.sh
  --dx_rt`, then `dx-runtime/install.sh --all --exclude-app --exclude-stream
  --skip-uninstall --venv-reuse` (dx_app/dx_stream NOT needed → skip to save time), retry.
  NPU init failure → cold boot. Never `pip install dx_engine` on x86-64 or fake via PYTHONPATH.

   - **Compilation-parallel workflow (HARD GATE)** — After launching `dxcom` or
     `dx_com.compile()` in a bash command, do NOT wait for it. Immediately

     run.sh, verify.py. Check `.dxnn` output only AFTER all other artifacts
     are created. **Violation of this rule fails the session.**
   - **NEVER sleep-poll for compilation** — Do NOT use `sleep` in a loop to
     poll for `.dxnn` files. Prohibited patterns include:
     `for i in ...; do sleep N; ls *.dxnn; done`,
     `while ! ls *.dxnn; do sleep N; done`,
     repeated `ls *.dxnn` / `test -f *.dxnn` checks with waits between them.
     Instead: generate all other artifacts first, then check ONCE whether the
     `.dxnn` file exists. If it does not exist yet, proceed to execution
     verification with the assumption that compilation will complete.
   - **NEVER use `pgrep -f` to monitor compile.pid process** — `pgrep -f
     "path/to/compile.py"` matches the bash shell that is running the pgrep
     command itself, causing an **infinite loop** that never exits even after
     compilation finishes. Always use `kill -0 <PID>` to check if a specific
     PID is still alive:
     ```bash
     # CORRECT — check by PID, not by name
     COMPILE_PID=$(cat compile.pid)
     while kill -0 "$COMPILE_PID" 2>/dev/null; do sleep 10; done
     echo "Compilation PID=$COMPILE_PID has exited"
     ```
     **Prohibited patterns** (self-referential, cause infinite loops):
     ```bash
     while pgrep -f "compile.py" >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 20; done   # PROHIBITED
     pgrep -f "session_dir/compile.py"                                 # PROHIBITED
     ```
   - **Mandatory artifacts are compilation-independent** — `setup.sh`, `run.sh`,
     `verify.py`, factory, and app code do NOT require the `.dxnn` file to exist.
     Generate them using the known model name (e.g., `yolo26n.dxnn`) as a
     placeholder path. Only execution verification requires the actual `.dxnn`.

   agent docs, or skill docs that are already loaded in your context. Each

## Rule Conflict Resolution (HARD GATE)

When a user's request conflicts with a HARD GATE rule, the agent MUST:

1. **Acknowledge the user's intent** — Show that you understand what they want.
2. **Explain the conflict** — Cite the specific rule and why it exists.
3. **Propose the correct alternative** — Show how to achieve the user's goal
   within the framework. For example, if the user asks for direct
   `InferenceEngine.run()` usage, explain that the IFactory pattern wraps
   the same API and propose the factory-based equivalent.
4. **Proceed with the correct approach** — Do NOT silently comply with the
   rule-violating request. Do NOT present it as "Option A vs Option B".

**Common conflict patterns** (from real sessions):
- User says "use `InferenceEngine.Run()`" → Must use IFactory pattern (engine
  calls are handled internally by SyncRunner/AsyncRunner; implement the 5 IFactory
  methods: `create_preprocessor`, `create_postprocessor`, `create_visualizer`,
  `get_model_name`, `get_task_type`)
- User says "clone demo.py and swap onnxruntime" → Must use skeleton-first
  from `src/python_example/`, not clone user scripts
- User says "create demo_dxnn_sync.py" → Must use `<model>_sync.py` naming
  with SyncRunner, not a standalone script
- User says "use `run_async()` directly" → Must use AsyncRunner, not manual
  async loops

**This rule does NOT override explicit user overrides**: If the user, after being
informed of the conflict, explicitly says "I understand the rule, proceed with
direct API usage anyway", then comply. But the agent MUST explain the conflict
FIRST — silent compliance is always a violation.

   ```
6. **NEVER output DONE after only producing planning artifacts** (specs, plans, design
   documents). DONE means all deliverables are produced — implementation code, scripts,
   configs, and validation results. If you completed a brainstorming or planning phase
   but have not yet implemented the actual code, do NOT output DONE. Instead, proceed
   to implementation or ask the user how to proceed.
7. **Pre-DONE mandatory deliverable check**: Before outputting DONE, verify that all
   mandatory deliverables exist in the session directory. If any mandatory file is
   missing, create it before outputting DONE. Each sub-project defines its own mandatory
   file list in its skill document (e.g., `dx-agentic-stream-build-pipeline.md` File Creation Checklist).
8. **Session transcript — generate it RIGHT AFTER the DONE line (claude / copilot)**:

   **Auto-transcript is supported on `claude` and `copilot` only.** Emit the DONE
   sentinel line FIRST, then — as the single final housekeeping step — render this
   session's transcript with the shared generator **directly into the session output
   dir(s)** (the same dir(s) you listed in DONE). Running it *after* DONE means the
   CLI's session store has already committed the DONE turn, so the rendered transcript
   is complete (rendering *before* DONE truncates the tail). Needs **no hook**:

   ```bash
   # Locate the shared generator by walking up to the suite root: GENROOT is the dir
   # that contains .deepx/tools. Then render THIS session's transcript INTO the session
   # output dir(s). Pass EVERY output dir you created (the transcript is copied into each
   # — cross-project: both the compiler and app dirs). The session id is auto-resolved
   # from this CLI's own env var (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID / COPILOT_AGENT_SESSION_ID).
   #
   # CRITICAL — use ABSOLUTE paths for --project AND --into-output-dirs. A RELATIVE
   # output dir is resolved against the agent's CURRENT cwd, so it is SILENTLY SKIPPED
   # ("no output dir produced — transcript generation skipped") whenever cwd is not the
   # suite root — e.g. after you cd into the session dir to run setup.sh/run.sh. Prefix
   # every output dir with "$GENROOT/" (or pass the same absolute SESSION_DIR you used
   # to write artifacts).
   GENROOT="$(d="$PWD"; while [ "$d" != / ]; do [ -f "$d/.deepx/tools/src/dx_transcripts/generate_transcripts.py" ] && { echo "$d"; break; }; d="$(dirname "$d")"; done)"
   GT="$GENROOT/.deepx/tools/src/dx_transcripts/generate_transcripts.py"
   python3 "$GT" --tool <CLI> --project "$GENROOT" \
       --into-output-dirs "$GENROOT/<output-dir>" ["$GENROOT/<output-dir-2>" ...]
   ```

   `<CLI>` is `claude` or `copilot`. The generator reuses the **same renderers as the
   test harness** (`parse_<tool>_session`) and writes `<CLI>-session.md` +
   `<CLI>-session.html` + `<CLI>-stream.jsonl` into each output dir. **If you produced
   NO output dir** (e.g. a pure question with no files), pass no dir and generation is
   **skipped** — expected, not an error. After it runs, state the path on the final
   line, e.g. `Session transcript (md/html/jsonl) saved to: <output-dir>/<CLI>-session.*`.

   > **Known limitation — the in-session transcript is store-based and therefore
   > incomplete.** Run from inside the live session, the generator reads the session
   > **store**, which has NO synthetic `result` event — that event (carrying
   > `duration_ms` → *Wall-clock* and `total_cost_usd` → *Cost*) exists only in the
   > `claude -p --output-format stream-json` **stdout**, emitted at process exit. The
   > render also happens *during* the transcript tool-call, so it truncates just before
   > this very "saved to …" narration. Net effect: the in-session transcript **omits
   > Wall-clock + Cost and the closing narration** — expected, not a bug. For a
   > **complete** transcript (Wall-clock + Cost + tail, like the showcase ones),
   > capture the run's stdout and render it externally **after** the process exits:
   > `python3 "$GT" --tool <CLI> --session-id <uuid> --project "$GENROOT" --stream-json <captured-stdout.jsonl> --out-dir <output-dir>`
   > (the test harness / build recorders do this). An in-session agent cannot — it has
   > no handle on its own stdout stream.

   **`codex`, `opencode`, `cursor` are NOT auto-supported** — do NOT run the generator
   in-session for them (it cannot produce a complete/usable transcript: codex and
   opencode commit their final turn only at process exit; cursor redacts the assistant
   text in its store). Instead, tell the user how to generate it manually:
   - **codex / opencode**: after the session ends, run
     `python3 <generate_transcripts.py> --tool <codex|opencode> --project . --out-dir <DIR>`
     — the finalized store then renders a complete transcript.
   - **cursor**: capture the run with `agent -p --output-format stream-json > run.jsonl`
     and render with `--tool cursor --stream-json run.jsonl`, or use IDE session history.
   (If you invoke the generator with `--into-output-dirs` on these tools, it safely
   skips and prints this same guidance — that is expected.)

## Plan Output (MANDATORY)

When generating a plan document (e.g., via writing-plans or brainstorming skills),
**always print the full plan content in the conversation output** immediately after
saving the file. Do NOT only mention the file path — the user should be able to
review the plan directly in the prompt without opening a separate file.


---

## Instruction File Verification Loop (HARD GATE) — Internal Development Only

When modifying the canonical source — files in `**/.deepx/**/*.md`
(agents, skills, templates, fragments) — the following verify-fix loop is
**MANDATORY** before claiming work is complete:

1. **Generator execution** — Propagate `.deepx/` changes to all platforms:
   ```bash
   dx-agentic-gen generate
   # Suite-wide: bash .deepx/tools/scripts/run_all.sh generate
   ```
2. **Drift verification** — Confirm generated output matches committed state:
   ```bash
   dx-agentic-gen check
   ```
   If drift is detected, return to step 1.
3. **Automated test loop** — Tests verify generator output satisfies policies:
   ```bash
   python -m pytest .deepx/tests/conformance/ .deepx/tools/tests/ -v --tb=short
   ```
   Failure handling:
   - Generator bug → fix generator → step 1
   - `.deepx/` content gap → fix `.deepx/` → step 1
   - Insufficient test rules → strengthen tests → step 1
4. **Manual audit** — Independently (without relying on test results) read
   generated files to verify cross-platform sync (CLAUDE vs AGENTS vs copilot)
   and level-to-level sync (suite → sub-levels).
5. **Gap analysis** — For issues found by manual audit:
   - Generator missed a case → **fix generator rules** → step 1
   - Tests missed a case → **strengthen tests** → step 1
6. **Repeat** — Continue until steps 3–5 all pass.

### Pre-flight Classification (MANDATORY)

Before modifying ANY `.md` or `.mdc` file in the repository, classify it into
one of three categories. **Never skip this step** — editing a generator-managed
file directly is a silent corruption that will be overwritten on next generate.

**Answer these three questions in order before every file edit:**

> **Q1. Is the file path inside `**/.deepx/**`?**
> - YES → **Canonical source.** Edit directly, then run `dx-agentic-gen generate` + `check`.
> - NO → go to Q2.
>
> **Q2. Does the file path or name match any of these?**
> ```
> .github/agents/    .github/skills/    .opencode/agents/
> .claude/agents/    .claude/skills/    .cursor/rules/
> CLAUDE.md          CLAUDE-KO.md       AGENTS.md    AGENTS-KO.md
> copilot-instructions.md               copilot-instructions-KO.md
> ```
> - YES → **Generator output. DO NOT edit directly.**
>   Find the `.deepx/` source (template, fragment, or agent/skill) and edit that instead,
>   then run `dx-agentic-gen generate`.
> - NO → go to Q3.
>
> **Q3. Does the file begin with `<!-- AUTO-GENERATED`?**
> - YES → **Generator output. DO NOT edit directly.** Same as Q2.
> - NO → **Independent source.** Edit directly. Run `dx-agentic-gen check` once afterward.

1. **Canonical source** (`**/.deepx/**/*.md`) — Modify directly, then run the
   Verification Loop above.
2. **Generator output** — Files at known output paths:
   `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE-KO.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS-KO.md`,
   `copilot-instructions.md`, `.github/agents/`, `.github/skills/`,
   `.claude/agents/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.opencode/agents/`, `.cursor/rules/`
   → **Do NOT edit directly.** Find and modify the `.deepx/` source
   (template, fragment, or agent/skill), then `dx-agentic-gen generate`.
3. **Independent source** — Everything else (`docs/source/`, `source/docs/`,
   `tests/`, `README.md` in sub-projects, etc.)
   → Edit directly. Run `dx-agentic-gen check` once afterward to confirm no
   unexpected drift.

**Anti-pattern**: Modifying a file without first classifying it. If you are
unsure whether a file is generator output, run `dx-agentic-gen check` before
AND after the edit — if the check overwrites your change, the file is managed
by the generator and must be edited via `.deepx/` source instead.

A pre-commit hook enforces generator output integrity: `git commit` will fail
if generated files are out-of-date. Install hooks with:
```bash
.deepx/tools/scripts/install-hooks.sh
```

> **KO counterpart rule**: When editing any EN fragment, check whether the KO
> counterpart also needs updating. If you added or removed ≥ 1 paragraph, update
> `.deepx/templates/fragments/ko/<stem>.md` before committing. Run
> `dx-agentic-gen lint` to verify `[OK]` — lint will ERROR if EN exceeds KO by
> ≥ 10 lines.

This gate applies when `.deepx/` files are the *primary deliverable* (e.g., adding
rules, syncing platforms, creating KO translations, modifying agents/skills). It
does NOT apply when a feature implementation incidentally triggers a single-line
change in `.deepx/`.

1	# Ultralytics Retrain + Evaluate (domain optimization) → DeepX
2	
3	> How to **adapt a base YOLO model to a specific domain** with the Ultralytics Python
4	> package and **evaluate it fairly** — both the PyTorch model (fp32) and its DeepX
5	> `.dxnn` (INT8 on DX-M1). Pairs with [`ultralytics-deepx-export.md`](./ultralytics-deepx-export.md)
6	> (the `format=deepx` compile step). Use this for "retrain on my dataset / optimize for
7	> my domain / measure accuracy + FPS" requests.
8	
9	> **Get the latest knowledge first (do not fabricate APIs).** Ultralytics evolves. Before
10	> writing training/eval code, read the current docs:
11	> - Local clone (preferred): `git clone https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics` then read
12	>   `docs/en/modes/train.md`, `docs/en/modes/val.md`, `docs/en/modes/benchmark.md`,
13	>   `docs/en/datasets/detect/*.md`, and `ultralytics/cfg/datasets/*.yaml`.
14	> - Or web search "ultralytics train mode" / "ultralytics val mAP" / the dataset name.
15	> The snippets below are a current-as-of-2026-06 snapshot; verify against the above.
16	
17	## The base model and its domain
18	
19	Stock `yolo26n.pt` (like other Ultralytics release weights) is **COCO-pretrained** — 80
20	general everyday-object classes (person, car, dog, …). It is a *general-purpose* detector
21	and performs poorly on **domain-specific** classes it never saw (e.g. wildlife species,
22	defect types, PCB components). Domain optimization = **fine-tune on a labeled dataset of
23	the target domain** so the model detects the domain's classes.
24	
25	## 1. Dataset (YAML)
26	
27	Detection datasets use an Ultralytics YAML (`path`, `train`, `val`, `nc`, `names`):
28	
29	```yaml
30	# my_domain.yaml
31	path: /abs/or/rel/dataset_root
32	train: images/train
33	val: images/val
34	nc: 4
35	names: [buffalo, elephant, rhino, zebra]
36	```
37	
38	- **Built-in datasets auto-download** on first use (no manual download): e.g.
39	  `african-wildlife.yaml`, `brain-tumor.yaml`, `signature.yaml`, `VOC.yaml`, `coco128.yaml`.
40	  Their YAMLs live in `ultralytics/cfg/datasets/`.
41	- **Custom dataset**: point `data=` at your own YAML; images in `images/`, YOLO-format
42	  labels (`class cx cy w h`, normalized) in `labels/` mirroring the split dirs.
43	
44	## 2. Retrain (fine-tune) on the domain — local GPU
45	
46	```python
47	from ultralytics import YOLO
48	
49	model = YOLO("yolo26n.pt")                      # base COCO weights
50	results = model.train(
51	    data="african-wildlife.yaml",               # or your custom my_domain.yaml
52	    epochs=40,                                   # modest count fine-tunes quickly
53	    imgsz=640,
54	    batch=16,
55	    device=0,                                    # local GPU; "cpu" if none
56	)
57	# best weights: runs/detect/train*/weights/best.pt
58	```
59	
60	```bash
61	yolo detect train model=yolo26n.pt data=african-wildlife.yaml epochs=40 imgsz=640 device=0
62	```
63	
64	The retrained head has `nc = <#domain classes>` (e.g. 4) instead of COCO's 80.
65	
66	## 3. Evaluate accuracy (mAP) — `model.val()`
67	
68	```python
69	m = YOLO("runs/detect/train/weights/best.pt").val(data="african-wildlife.yaml", imgsz=640)
70	print(m.box.map, m.box.map50, m.box.map75)      # mAP50-95, mAP50, mAP75
71	print(m.box.maps)                                # per-class mAP50-95
72	# m.speed -> {'preprocess','inference','postprocess'} ms/img → FPS = 1000/inference
73	```
74	
75	- **mAP50-95** is the primary accuracy metric; report mAP50 + per-class too.
76	- **FPS** = `1000 / m.speed["inference"]` (single-image latency), measured on an idle host.
77	
78	## 4. Export to DeepX + evaluate the `.dxnn`
79	
80	Export each `.pt` with `format=deepx` (see `ultralytics-deepx-export.md`), then run the
81	**same `model.val()`** on the exported model directory — the Ultralytics DeepX backend
82	runs INT8 inference on the DX-M1 NPU, so the reported mAP/FPS are the on-device numbers:
83	
84	```python
85	YOLO("yolo26n.pt").export(format="deepx")                       # → yolo26n_deepx_model/
86	m = YOLO("yolo26n_deepx_model").val(data="african-wildlife.yaml", imgsz=640)  # NPU mAP+FPS
87	```
88	
89	## 5. The fair comparison (base vs retrained × fp32 vs INT8)
90	
91	For a domain-optimization report, measure **four** points so accuracy *and* the
92	quantization effect are both visible:
93	
94	| Model | Form | Device | What it shows |
95	|---|---|---|---|
96	| base `yolo26n` | `.pt` (fp32) | GPU | the general model's domain accuracy (usually ~0 on unseen classes) |
97	| base `yolo26n` | `.dxnn` (INT8) | DX-M1 NPU | on-device baseline FPS/accuracy |
98	| retrained | `.pt` (fp32) | GPU | the upper-bound domain accuracy after fine-tuning |
99	| retrained | `.dxnn` (INT8) | DX-M1 NPU | the deployable result; INT8 vs fp32 gap = quantization loss |
100	
101	Report Δaccuracy (retrain vs base) and Δspeed; note that a smaller `nc` head often makes
102	the domain `.dxnn` **faster** on the NPU than the 80-class stock model.
103	
104	## Constraints / notes
105	
106	- Export/compile is **x86-64 Linux only**; **detection** task; **INT8 enforced** (see
107	  `ultralytics-deepx-export.md`). Training itself runs on GPU/CPU on any platform.
108	- `dx_engine` (for NPU `.dxnn` eval) is a **dx_rt** artifact — build dx-runtime
109	  (`install.sh --all --exclude-app --exclude-stream`), not pip. See the deploy section of
110	  `ultralytics-deepx-export.md`.
111	
112	## References
113	
114	- Ultralytics: `docs/en/modes/train.md`, `val.md`, `benchmark.md`, `docs/en/datasets/detect/`
115	- DeepX export: `ultralytics-deepx-export.md` · compile: `dxcom-cli.md`/`dxcom-api.md`

# Ultralytics Retrain + Evaluate (domain optimization) → DeepX

> How to **adapt a base YOLO model to a specific domain** with the Ultralytics Python
> package and **evaluate it fairly** — both the PyTorch model (fp32) and its DeepX
> `.dxnn` (INT8 on DX-M1). Pairs with [`ultralytics-deepx-export.md`](./ultralytics-deepx-export.md)
> (the `format=deepx` compile step). Use this for "retrain on my dataset / optimize for
> my domain / measure accuracy + FPS" requests.

> **Get the latest knowledge first (do not fabricate APIs).** Ultralytics evolves. Before
> writing training/eval code, read the current docs:
> - Local clone (preferred): `git clone https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics` then read
>   `docs/en/modes/train.md`, `docs/en/modes/val.md`, `docs/en/modes/benchmark.md`,
>   `docs/en/datasets/detect/*.md`, and `ultralytics/cfg/datasets/*.yaml`.
> - Or web search "ultralytics train mode" / "ultralytics val mAP" / the dataset name.
> The snippets below are a current-as-of-2026-06 snapshot; verify against the above.

## The base model and its domain

Stock `yolo26n.pt` (like other Ultralytics release weights) is **COCO-pretrained** — 80
general everyday-object classes (person, car, dog, …). It is a *general-purpose* detector
and performs poorly on **domain-specific** classes it never saw (e.g. wildlife species,
defect types, PCB components). Domain optimization = **fine-tune on a labeled dataset of
the target domain** so the model detects the domain's classes.

## 1. Dataset (YAML)

Detection datasets use an Ultralytics YAML (`path`, `train`, `val`, `nc`, `names`):

```yaml
# my_domain.yaml
path: /abs/or/rel/dataset_root
train: images/train
val: images/val
nc: 4
names: [buffalo, elephant, rhino, zebra]
```

- **Built-in datasets auto-download** on first use (no manual download): e.g.
  `african-wildlife.yaml`, `brain-tumor.yaml`, `signature.yaml`, `VOC.yaml`, `coco128.yaml`.
  Their YAMLs live in `ultralytics/cfg/datasets/`.
- **Custom dataset**: point `data=` at your own YAML; images in `images/`, YOLO-format
  labels (`class cx cy w h`, normalized) in `labels/` mirroring the split dirs.

## 2. Retrain (fine-tune) on the domain — local GPU

```python
from ultralytics import YOLO

model = YOLO("yolo26n.pt")                      # base COCO weights
results = model.train(
    data="african-wildlife.yaml",               # or your custom my_domain.yaml
    epochs=40,                                   # modest count fine-tunes quickly
    imgsz=640,
    batch=16,
    device=0,                                    # local GPU; "cpu" if none
)
# best weights: runs/detect/train*/weights/best.pt
```

```bash
yolo detect train model=yolo26n.pt data=african-wildlife.yaml epochs=40 imgsz=640 device=0
```

The retrained head has `nc = <#domain classes>` (e.g. 4) instead of COCO's 80.

## 3. Evaluate accuracy (mAP) — `model.val()`

```python
m = YOLO("runs/detect/train/weights/best.pt").val(data="african-wildlife.yaml", imgsz=640)
print(m.box.map, m.box.map50, m.box.map75)      # mAP50-95, mAP50, mAP75
print(m.box.maps)                                # per-class mAP50-95
# m.speed -> {'preprocess','inference','postprocess'} ms/img → FPS = 1000/inference
```

- **mAP50-95** is the primary accuracy metric; report mAP50 + per-class too.
- **FPS** = `1000 / m.speed["inference"]` (single-image latency), measured on an idle host.

## 4. Export to DeepX + evaluate the `.dxnn`

Export each `.pt` with `format=deepx` (see `ultralytics-deepx-export.md`), then run the
**same `model.val()`** on the exported model directory — the Ultralytics DeepX backend
runs INT8 inference on the DX-M1 NPU, so the reported mAP/FPS are the on-device numbers:

```python
YOLO("yolo26n.pt").export(format="deepx")                       # → yolo26n_deepx_model/
m = YOLO("yolo26n_deepx_model").val(data="african-wildlife.yaml", imgsz=640)  # NPU mAP+FPS
```

## 5. The fair comparison (base vs retrained × fp32 vs INT8)

For a domain-optimization report, measure **four** points so accuracy *and* the
quantization effect are both visible:

| Model | Form | Device | What it shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| base `yolo26n` | `.pt` (fp32) | GPU | the general model's domain accuracy (usually ~0 on unseen classes) |
| base `yolo26n` | `.dxnn` (INT8) | DX-M1 NPU | on-device baseline FPS/accuracy |
| retrained | `.pt` (fp32) | GPU | the upper-bound domain accuracy after fine-tuning |
| retrained | `.dxnn` (INT8) | DX-M1 NPU | the deployable result; INT8 vs fp32 gap = quantization loss |

Report Δaccuracy (retrain vs base) and Δspeed; note that a smaller `nc` head often makes
the domain `.dxnn` **faster** on the NPU than the 80-class stock model.

## Constraints / notes

- Export/compile is **x86-64 Linux only**; **detection** task; **INT8 enforced** (see
  `ultralytics-deepx-export.md`). Training itself runs on GPU/CPU on any platform.
- `dx_engine` (for NPU `.dxnn` eval) is a **dx_rt** artifact — build dx-runtime
  (`install.sh --all --exclude-app --exclude-stream`), not pip. See the deploy section of
  `ultralytics-deepx-export.md`.

## References

- Ultralytics: `docs/en/modes/train.md`, `val.md`, `benchmark.md`, `docs/en/datasets/detect/`
- DeepX export: `ultralytics-deepx-export.md` · compile: `dxcom-cli.md`/`dxcom-api.md`

1	# Ultralytics → DeepX Export Reference
2	
3	> One-shot `format=deepx` exporter built into Ultralytics YOLO. Converts a YOLO
4	> `.pt` to a deployable DeepX NPU model (`.dxnn`) in a single command —
5	> internally running ONNX export → INT8 EMA calibration → `dx_com` compilation →
6	> packaging. Use this BEFORE hand-rolling the PT→ONNX→`dxcom` pipeline for
7	> Ultralytics YOLO **detection** models.
8	
9	## When to use this path (decision matrix)
10	
11	| Situation | Path |
12	|---|---|
13	| Ultralytics YOLO **detection** model (`.pt`) → DeepX NPU | **`format=deepx` one-shot** (this doc) |
14	| Non-detection task (seg/pose/cls/obb), or export currently unsupported | Manual PT→ONNX (`dx-agentic-compiler-convert`) → `dxcom` (`dxcom-cli.md`) |
15	| Arbitrary / non-YOLO ONNX, custom graph, or fine control over config.json | Direct `dxcom` / `dx_com.compile()` (`dxcom-api.md`, `config-schema.md`) |
16	| Already have a clean `.onnx` and just need `.dxnn` | Direct `dxcom` |
17	
18	The one-shot path is preferred for the YOLO-detection→DeepX case because it
19	handles ONNX export quirks (single-output graph), INT8 calibration, and `dx_com`
20	invocation automatically — eliminating the most common manual-pipeline errors.
21	
22	## Platform constraints (HARD)
23	
24	- **x86-64 Linux only** for the export/compile step — `dx_com` does **not**
25	  support ARM64/aarch64. Always export on an x86-64 Linux host.
26	- **Detection models only** (current release). Other tasks may be added later.
27	- **INT8 is enforced** — `int8=True` is set automatically; passing `int8=False`
28	  is overridden with a warning. There is no FP16/FP32 DeepX output.
29	- Target NPU is **DX-M1** (`dx_m1`), consistent with the rest of dx-compiler.
30	
31	## Installation
32	
33	```bash
34	pip install ultralytics
35	# dx_com (the compiler) is pulled in automatically on the first `format=deepx` export.
36	```
37	
38	> **dx_engine is NOT pip-auto-installed in the DEEPX suite.** Ultralytics' upstream
39	> doc says the runtime "installs automatically," but inside dx-all-suite the
40	> `dx_engine` inference runtime is a **build artifact of `dx-runtime/dx_app`**, not a
41	> PyPI package. Export (compile) needs only `ultralytics` + `dx_com`; **deployment**
42	> (running the exported model) needs `dx_engine` from a built dx-runtime. See
43	> "Deployment prerequisites" below before the deploy step.
44	
45	## Export — API and CLI
46	
47	```python
48	from ultralytics import YOLO
49	
50	model = YOLO("yolo26n.pt")            # load (auto-downloads from Ultralytics if absent)
51	model.export(format="deepx")          # creates 'yolo26n_deepx_model/' (int8=True enforced)
52	```
53	
54	```bash
55	# CLI equivalent
56	yolo export model=yolo26n.pt format=deepx     # creates 'yolo26n_deepx_model/'
57	```
58	
59	### Export arguments
60	
61	| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
62	|---|---|---|---|
63	| `format` | str | `'deepx'` | Target format — DeepX NPU. |

72	hundred rarely improves accuracy. Tune via `data` / `fraction`.

88

90	integration (verified against `ultralytics/utils/export/deepx.py` and
91	`ultralytics/nn/backends/deepx.py`):
92	
93	| Component | Who installs it | How |
94	|---|---|---|
95	| `dx_com` (compiler, **export**) | **Ultralytics auto-installs** | on first `format=deepx`, Ultralytics' own `check_requirements("dx_com", …)` pip-installs it from the DeepX SDK index. **The version is pinned inside the installed `ultralytics` release and tracks it** — upgrading `ultralytics` upgrades the pin. |

99	> version string embedded in Ultralytics' `check_requirements` call (e.g. a
100	> `…/dxcom/vX.Y.Z/index.html` URL) belongs to that ultralytics release — copying it
101	> into a manual `pip install -f …` pins a **stale** compiler. Let
102	> `model.export(format="deepx")` install `dx_com` itself; to update, upgrade
103	> `ultralytics`. (The standalone direct-`dxcom` path is a separate workflow — there,
104	> use the normal `pip install dx-com`; see `dxcom-cli.md`.)
105	
106	So **export needs only `ultralytics` (+ auto `dx_com`)**, but **deploy needs the
107	DeepX runtime present**. On a non-Debian-Trixie-arm64 host — including the standard
108	**x86-64 dx-all-suite** — the Ultralytics backend does NOT auto-install the runtime;
109	it raises one of these and stops:

113	OSError: DeepX runtime auto-install is only supported on Debian Trixie (arm64).
114	OSError: dx_engine is not installed. Auto-install is only supported on Debian Trixie (arm64). Please install dx_engine manually and try again.
115	```

118	context means: install the `dx_rt` runtime**, which provides BOTH `dxrt-cli` and the
119	`dx_engine` Python module. **`dx_app` and `dx_stream` are NOT needed** for Ultralytics
120	export/deploy — `dx_engine` is a `dx_rt` artifact, not a `dx_app` one — so exclude
121	them to save build time. Do NOT `pip install dx_engine` on x86-64 and do NOT fake the
122	import via `PYTHONPATH`/`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` — both are prohibited bypasses:
123	
124	```bash

126	#    PASS = "Sanity check PASSED!" and NO [ERROR] lines. Never pipe through tail/head/grep.

130	#    --exclude-app --exclude-stream skips the unneeded app/stream builds):
131	python -c "import dx_engine; print('dx_engine OK')" 2>/dev/null || {
132	    bash dx-runtime/install.sh --all --exclude-app --exclude-stream --skip-uninstall --venv-reuse
133	    bash dx-runtime/scripts/sanity_check.sh --dx_rt   # MUST PASS, then re-run inference
134	}
135	```
136	
137	- If `sanity_check.sh` reports **"Device initialization failed" / NPU hardware
138	  error**, software install cannot fix it — the NPU needs a **cold boot** (full power
139	  cycle), then re-run the sanity check. STOP and tell the user; do not bypass.
140	- This mirrors the suite-level **Prerequisites Check (HARD GATE)** and **Sanity Check
141	  Failure Recovery** in the top-level `CLAUDE.md`; apply them when a deploy step is
142	  requested, even though the task routed through dx-compiler.
